09:15 PDT. EPIC COMPLETE. wide-wimpy-insect (87cb) closed, all six children closed, all six Gerrit changes MERGED (2503, 2504, 2505, 2506, 2507, 2510). Mechanism ratchet green on merged main: active=682 new=0 increased=0 stale=0.

The final stretch, and what the gates caught:

* b0ac refused TWICE more. First for scope: the merged commit touched src/rebar/_store/fsutil.py and docs/concurrency.md, neither declared in file_impact -- both were the AC6 documentation work. Widened to 9 paths. The re-review then BLOCKED on a real accuracy defect: the plan's site table cited _snapshot/janitor.py:300 for the integrity-stamp write, but line 300 is `_cache.add_bytes(-size, root)` in an EVICTION path; the actual atomic_write is in reverify_entry() (line 365), and completion_banking's was in upsert() (511, cited as 507). Fixed by anchoring both locators to FUNCTION NAMES rather than line numbers, so they cannot rot again. Re-review PASS + signed, closed.

* The epic close needed its own re-review first: editing four children's plans during the session drifted the epic's pinned child material (stale-pin-drift on 0880, 9ca8, b0ac, f9b9). Re-review PASS + signed. Then the close refused on the epic's OWN seven unticked ACs. I verified all seven against the merged tree before ticking any -- AC1 parity gate in make lint with its seeded-mismatch test; AC2 mirror inventory tracked; AC3 proven by tests/unit/test_collection_isolation_guard.py with conftest raising UsageError from pytest_collection_modifyitems, i.e. genuinely at collection time; AC4 test_unique_cache_writes.py; AC5 ratchet in make lint against the committed baseline; AC6 three reports plus ADR 0110; AC7 --help live on both shipped check scripts. Ticking left the attestation `certified`, confirming again that box state is normalized out of the fingerprint while AC TEXT edits are material.

Note for the record: five of the six commits merged while I was blocked on the outage, so the subagent's rebase legitimately reduced the stack to one commit by patch-id -- not history rewriting. It also corrected an instruction of mine: check_mechanism_delta.py has no --lock flag (only --check and --update-stale, and --update-stale refuses to write while new>0 by design), so it regenerated the baseline through the script's own census()+render_baseline() path. 681 -> 682 entries.

Separately filed and linked: cyclopean-bloodshot-hoatzin (3276-2f81-8c75-4ddd), priority 1, for the root-disk outage that blocked this work for ~5 hours -- still OPEN, six relates_to links to prior failed attempts, and it carries the measured reason those attempts could not have worked.
